scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The TPO terminal (192.168.3.5) reports they cannot reach any
Internet Lab PC (128.168.0.x). At the same time, every PC in
the IT Department and CS Department reports they cannot reach
ANYTHING outside their own department. The Principle Room and
Other zone can still reach the Server Room and Internet Lab
normally. Find what broke.

injection.action: bring down the WAN-side link to router0

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1's Serial2/0 (eth2) interface, the
  10.10.0.0/8 link between router0 and router1
Mechanism: router0 is the gateway for IT (192.168.1.0/24)
  and CS (192.168.2.0/24). It only reaches the rest of the
  network (router1, router2, all their attached subnets) via
  the Serial link to router1. With that link down, RIP on
  router1 ages out 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, and
  router0 ages out everything else. The TPO->128.168.0.2
  path is router1 -> router2 -> Switch5, which does NOT
  cross the down link, so it stays up.
Localization: router1 eth2 (or router0 eth2 — both ends of
  the 10.10.0.0/8 link)
Root cause: WAN link router0<->router1 (10.10.0.0/8) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The WAN interface **router1 eth2** (the link on the `wan_r0_r1` segment connecting router1 to router0) was brought down. FRR records exactly one link-up event at 13:32:15 followed by one link-down event at 13:33:45 — roughly 90 seconds after lab startup — and the interface has remained down since, with no `LOWER_UP` flag in the kernel.

The mechanism is a cascade through RIP. While eth2 was briefly UP, router1 sent RIP updates to router0 and router0 learned remote prefixes (Internet 128.168.0.0/16, Office 192.168.3.0/24, Principle 192.168.4.0/24, etc.). The moment eth2 went DOWN, router1 stopped sending RIP hellos on that interface. RIP's 180-second garbage-collection timer fired on router0, and all remotely learned routes were purged. Router0's FIB now contains only its three directly connected networks (10.0.0.0/8 WAN stub, 192.168.1.0/24 IT, 192.168.2.0/24 CS). Any packet destined for the Internet, Server Room, Office, or Principle zones that arrives at router0 gets an immediate ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable" — confirmed by live pings from both `it_hod` and `cs_hod`. Meanwhile, router1 and router2 never had routes to 192.168.1.0/24 or 192.168.2.0/24 so the return path is equally broken. The TPO report is a misattribution: TPO reaches router1's still-UP eth0 and exits through the healthy eth3→router2 path; the ping to 128.168.0.2 succeeds with 0% loss.

**Root cause**: router1's eth2 was administratively shut down, severing the only WAN link between router0 and the rest of the topology.

**Fix**: On router1, run `ip link set eth2 up`. Once the interface returns to `LOWER_UP`, RIP will re-converge within one update interval (~30 s), restoring all routes on both router0 and router1/router2, and full IT/CS connectivity will be re-established.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names the router0–router1 WAN link (router1 eth2 on the wan_r0_r1 segment), which corresponds to the 10.10.0.0/8 affected link.

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only IT/CS are affected, not Other/Principle
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states that only IT/CS hosts (it_hod, cs_hod) see ICMP unreachable and that TPO/other paths (e.g. to 128.168.0.2) remain up, distinguishing the symptom pattern.
Recommends running 'ip link set eth2 up' on router1, which matches the expected remediation to restore the WAN link.

The agent's investigation is well supported by the log: interface eth2 on router1 was observed DOWN and remote routes disappeared, and host pings confirm the symptom. One minor unsupported wording (calling the interface 'administratively shut down') and not explicitly checking the peer's interface state reduce the perfection slightly.
